questions.q: Which best describes what statistics is for?
options: Learning from data while being honest about uncertainty
Producing a single exact answer from any dataset
Replacing the need to collect data
Making charts look more professional
questions.explain: Statistics summarizes data, infers beyond it, and attaches an honest measure of uncertainty to conclusions.

questions.q: What is the difference between a population and a sample?
options: A sample is the whole group; a population is a subset
A population is the complete group of interest; a sample is the part you actually measured
They are the same thing with different names
A population is always numeric; a sample is always categorical
questions.explain: The population is everyone or everything you care about; a sample is the part you observed.

questions.q: In the lesson, three samples of 50 orders gave means of 60.7, 58.77 and 58.38 while the population mean was 60.44. What does this show?
options: The code has a bug
Sample means vary from sample to sample, so a sample mean is an estimate, not the truth
Samples of 50 are always useless
The population mean must be wrong
questions.explain: This is sampling variability: each random sample is a slightly different slice of the population.

questions.q: Which task is an example of inferential rather than descriptive statistics?
options: Reporting the average order value in this month's data
Drawing a histogram of last week's orders
Using a sample of customers to estimate the average spend of all future customers
Counting how many rows are in a table
questions.explain: Inference goes beyond the observed data to say something about a larger group.

questions.q: Why can't a data scientist just report one sample average as 'the answer'?
options: Averages are never useful
Because the sample average will always be exactly the population average
Because a different random sample would likely give a different average, so we need to quantify how far to trust it
Because statistics forbids reporting averages
questions.explain: Since samples wobble, a responsible analysis reports how uncertain the estimate is.
